purpose: Sodium bicarbonate is used to relieve heartburn, acid indigestion, and upset stomach by neutralizing excess stomach acid. It is also used to make the urine less acidic, which can help treat certain kidney conditions and prevent kidney stones. In hospitals, it may be given through an IV to correct dangerously low blood pH (acidosis).
how_it_works: Think of sodium bicarbonate as a natural neutralizer — it works like baking soda to calm down excess acid in your stomach or bloodstream. When it mixes with stomach acid, it creates a chemical reaction that reduces acidity quickly, helping you feel better fast. It also helps your kidneys flush out certain substances more easily by making your urine less acidic.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include gas, bloating, and burping (from the reaction with stomach acid). You may also notice increased thirst or mild nausea. If used too often, it can cause a condition called metabolic alkalosis, where your blood becomes too basic, leading to muscle twitching, headache, or confusion.
warnings: Do not use this medication regularly without talking to your doctor — it is meant for short-term relief only. If you are on a low-sodium diet, have high blood pressure, kidney disease, or heart problems, check with your doctor before using it because it contains sodium. Avoid taking it right after a large meal, as it can cause your stomach to rupture in rare cases. Tell your doctor about all your medications, as it can affect how other drugs are absorbed.
typical_dosing: For adults, a typical dose for heartburn is 1/2 teaspoon of baking soda dissolved in a glass of water (about 4–8 oz), taken every 2 hours as needed — but no more than 7 doses per day. For tablets or prepared products like Alka-Seltzer, follow the package directions. Always use the lowest effective dose and avoid using it for more than 2 weeks without medical guidance.
